decisions.choice: Android phone/tablet/TV, standalone Wear OS, packaged Windows, and Web.
One new KnC repository with the modules core/ (Kotlin Multiplatform common + jvm + android + js), content/, android/, wear/, desktop/, web/ and, when the leaderboard starts, server/.

CS-KMP-CORE. core/commonMain owns models, cells (VOID included), both generators, turn rules, skip/restart, scoring and the snapshot schema. Each client owns DI, rendering, input, persistence and store integration.

rejected.reason: Needs an Android View-to-Compose migration and the Beta Compose Web target (EV-02); it is not the simplest path.
Rewrites the rules in another language and has no Wear OS export.
Two Kotlin copies already drift (EV-10, WD-05); four copies multiply it.

decisions.choice: Copy the phone game sources (phone.models, phone.generator, phone.rules, phone.scoring, phone.snapshot) and the watch variants (wear.models, wear.generator, wear.rules) from the 2026-11-24 snapshot into core/, and the phone and watch UI into android/ and wear/. FMS_A and the FMS watch app are not changed.

Two gameType values in core: SQUARE_GROWING (phone board 8..20 by level, shadowCount = N, L-path corridor generator) and ROUND_FIXED (watch board 12x11 round or 10x9 compact with VOID corners, shadowCount = min(5, 2 + (N-1)/3), BFS corridor generator). Both are selectable on every platform. The Wear client keeps its round geometry as the default; the 9x9 watch square stays a board configuration of SQUARE_GROWING only if it reproduces that type's size rule, otherwise it is unranked.

Generators keep kotlin.random.Random(seed) (XorWow, implemented in Kotlin common code) and the exact call order of the baseline. A seed must give one board per gameType + board configuration + rulesVersion on every target; it is never compared across gameTypes. If the js target diverges on RC-GEN-05, replace the source with an explicit XorWow in commonMain and bump rulesVersion.

RS-CANONICAL-ASSETS: content/ holds vector art as SVG source, one string table and mods as data; a generator emits Android/Wear resources and desktop/web resources. Mods never carry code. Each build embeds a contentVersion and a content manifest hash.

Every channel publishes on its own schedule. Every build carries rulesVersion and contentVersion; a platform may lack a feature (capability flag per client) but never runs different rules under the same rulesVersion. No held simultaneous publish (CR-HELD-PUBLISH) and no remote activation in the first release.

CR-STALE-CLIENT: offline play works on any rulesVersion; once the leaderboard exists, the server accepts ranked runs only for active rulesVersion values per gameType and tells an older client to update. Rollback = re-activate the previous rulesVersion on the server and ship the previous client build; a run keeps the rulesVersion it was played under.

SR-OWN-SERVICE in server/, specified from the FMS Windows exchange server and started after the four apps. Key = gameType + boardConfiguration + rulesVersion (difficulty excluded). A run submits seed, gameType, boardConfiguration, rulesVersion, contentVersion and the move log; the server replays it with the JVM build of core and computes the score itself. A ranked run requires an unmodified rules content hash. Opening it changes the privacy page and every store data-safety form in the same release.

platforms.ui: Android Views ported from the FMS_A game screen (phone.board-view, phone.activity, phone.viewmodel).
platforms.build: Gradle Android application consuming core (android target).
platforms.distribution: Google Play under a new applicationId, frozen at Play Console app creation.
platforms.assetProvenance: content/ generator output; first version from the FMS_A game drawables and strings.

platforms.ui: Compose for Wear OS ported from the FMS watch game screen.
platforms.build: Gradle Wear application consuming core (android target), 64-bit.
platforms.distribution: Google Play, standalone Wear OS app (com.google.android.wearable.standalone=true), its own track and listing with a watch screenshot (EV-05, EV-06).

platforms.ui: Compose Desktop on JVM, new interface over core.
platforms.build: Gradle JVM desktop; jpackage EXE/MSI on a Windows host (EV-03); MSIX by makeappx or the MSIX Packaging Tool (EV-04).
platforms.distribution: Microsoft Store (MSIX identity frozen at reservation) and winget (PackageIdentifier frozen at first submission).
platforms.codeProvenance: core jvm target; no game logic in desktop/.

platforms.ui: Kotlin/JS (Stable) with an HTML canvas renderer; installable web app manifest.
platforms.build: Gradle Kotlin/JS browser distribution consuming core (js target).
platforms.distribution: Static hosting on an owned origin; origin and manifest id frozen at first publication.
platforms.codeProvenance: core js target; no game logic in web/.

acceptanceChecks.check: Each of the four modules builds a distributable for its channel named in platforms[].
The repository contains core/, content/, android/, wear/, desktop/, web/; no game rule exists outside core/.
core/commonTest runs every baseline referenceCase (RC-GEN-*, RC-TURN-*, RC-RST-*, RC-MODE-01, RC-VAL-01, RC-ADV-01) on the jvm, android and js targets and passes.
For each gameType, RC-GEN-05 and the per-type golden boards produce identical boards on jvm and js for the same seed, board configuration and rulesVersion.
Every client offers SQUARE_GROWING and ROUND_FIXED; the Wear client defaults to ROUND_FIXED; WD-01..WD-06 behaviour is reproduced inside ROUND_FIXED only.
No file under app_v2/ or wear/ of the FMS repository changes because of the standalone work.
Builds of one contentVersion report the same content manifest hash on all four platforms.
Each build exposes rulesVersion and contentVersion, and each saved run records both.
The leaderboard key is gameType + boardConfiguration + rulesVersion and ignores difficulty and platform.
The server recomputes the submitted score from the move log with core and rejects a mismatch or an inactive rulesVersion.
